Routes._comment: AuthenticationController is [AllowAnonymous] at the class level, no per-action override, for all 11 actions (login, verify-otp, resend-otp, refresh, change-password, change-default-password, forgot-password, reset-password, validate-reset-token, logout, financial-years) — confirmed by reading the controller directly, not assumed.

Added 2026-08-20 (found missing during live debugging - UBIS_Web's IAimClient.GetAppSettingsAsync was 404ing through the Gateway even though AIM itself served /api/app-settings fine directly). AppSettingsController is [AllowAnonymous] at the class level — confirmed by reading the controller; protected by CallerRestrictionMiddleware instead, same as MenuController.GetByRole below.
UserRoleController.GetMyRole has its own [Authorize] — confirmed by reading the controller. Listed before the userrole catch-all route since Ocelot matches more specific templates first.
UserRoleController.CheckPermission has its own [Authorize] — confirmed by reading the controller.

Everything else under userrole/* (all-roles, {userId}/role, roles/{roleId}, roles/{roleId}/functions) has no [Authorize] anywhere — confirmed by reading the controller, not a simplification. Known-open surface, same as it is calling AIM directly today; not something this gateway change makes more or less open.

Every action under api/users/* (split across UserLookupController and ComplianceController) is [Authorize] — confirmed action-by-action by reading both controllers; no anonymous action exists anywhere in this path.
MenuController.GetByRole is explicitly [AllowAnonymous] (internal-tooling endpoint, protected by CallerRestrictionMiddleware instead) — confirmed by reading the controller.

MenuController.GetFull requires [Authorize] via the class-level attribute (no per-action override) — confirmed by reading the controller. Catch-all also covers any future action added to this controller with a safe (auth-required) default.

Email has zero REST controllers (confirmed — pure RabbitMQ consumer, no *Controller.cs anywhere in the project). This route is currently vestigial/unreachable; kept for when a real HTTP surface (e.g. /health) is added, with a safe (auth-required) default.

LogController has no [Authorize]/[AllowAnonymous] at all — LogWriter doesn't validate JWTs (confirmed, no AddJwtBearer in its Program.cs); its only protection is CallerRestrictionMiddleware's shared-secret header, which the Gateway forwards (see Program.cs). No AuthenticationOptions here deliberately — there's no JWT concept on this service to check.

New 2026-07-23. Every controller in ReferenceData (SchemesController/MajorHeadsController/ObjectHeadsController) is [Authorize] at the class level, no anonymous actions — confirmed by reading them (built alongside this route).

New 2026-07-23. Every controller in PreBudget (AppendicesController/AutonomousBodiesController/RemarksController/AppendixIController/AppendixIIController/AppendixIIIAController) is [Authorize] at the class level, no anonymous actions — confirmed by reading them (built alongside this route). Only 3 of the 22 appendix-data controllers exist so far (I, II, III-A) — the remaining 19 follow the identical AppendixDataRepository<T> pattern and will land under this same route prefix.

New 2026-08-18. Both controllers in ECL (EclOutlayController/EclApprovalController) are [Authorize] at the class level, no anonymous actions — confirmed by reading them. EclApprovalController's approve/reject/reapproval-grant actions additionally check the caller's RoleId against DoeRoleOptions.DoeRoleIds server-side, independent of this gateway's own Bearer check.

New 2026-08-25 (Foundation stage — no controllers with real actions yet, /health is the only endpoint). SBE (Domain/SBE) is the Statement of Budget Estimates module; role gating for actions restricted to one of its 3 FRS roles (Ministry/Budget Division/ABO-DS-Director) is enforced server-side via RequireSbeRoleFilter, independent of this gateway's own Bearer check.

New 2026-08-20. Reporting (Core/Reporting) is a stateless PDF/Excel export service reused across any future consumer page — ReportsController is [Authorize] at the class level, no anonymous actions, no domain-specific knowledge of ECL/PreBudget/etc.
